chunk_findings.detail: The new guard returns `O.refused(...)` unconditionally whenever `OC.failed_ci_blockers(st, cfg, item)` reports a merge-blocking gate, with no consultation of any force / `--reason` escape. The stated contract of this change is that merge refuses only "unless --force with a reason", and the knob's own doc in `config_sections/gates.py` claims the only way past is "a run that passes" — so the documented `--force` hatch is absent from the very path that implements the refusal. Concrete case: an item whose `ci` latest outcome is FAILED because ci failed on golden snapshots that cannot be re-pinned (a lease holds them — the exact situation that produced B23bd81462d), and whose snapshot cannot be re-run to a pass. Invoking `ddflow merge <item> --force --reason "..."` reaches this line (it sits before `target = FS.target(...)` and before any later force handling in the same function), returns refused, and the item can never be landed: `gate skip` is now refused too, and a passing run is impossible, so the guard deadlocks the case it was written to fix rather than offering the prescribed override. Either this return must be guarded by the force flag (with the reason required), or force must short-circuit before the check.

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal of a skip over a failed required gate is bypassable by recording a hand pass instead. Input: a required `ci` gate (non-reviewer) whose latest outcome is FAILED, then `ddflow gate record <item> ci --outcome passed --reason "flaky"`. At the call site `hard_skip = skip or outcome == "skipped"` is `False` while `hand` is `True`, so the new branch is skipped entirely and the second guard returns `None` because `ci` has no reviewer — the pass is recorded. The latest `ci` outcome is now `passed`, which is neither `failed` nor `skipped-after-failure`, so the merge refusal (`gates.merge_blocked_by_failed`) does not trigger and no `--force --reason` is required; the merge proceeds and main goes red exactly as in B23bd81462d. The intent enumerates only `--outcome unavailable|partial` as the legitimate hand remedy for a failed required gate (plus "fix and re-run"), but the code routes every non-`failed` hand outcome through the same unguarded path, for agents and operators alike, so the `skipped`-laundering the change set out to stop is still available with a different verb. Note the function already carries `hand` (and the review-gate branch deliberately inspects hand-recorded passes), so the information needed to cover this case is present in the signature but unused by the new check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:_agent_skip_refusal (new `skip_over_failure_refusal` branch, ~line 996)

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard is an unconditional refusal: it consults only the recorded gate outcomes (`OC.failed_ci_blockers(st, cfg, item)`) and never the force/reason inputs. The stated intent for this change is that merge refuses "unless `--force` with a reason", and the escape hatch is the whole point of the fix (the very scenario it was filed from — ci failed on four golden snapshots that could not be re-pinned because a lease held them — is one an operator would legitimately want to land with `--force --reason`). Given item `X` whose ci latest outcome is FAILED (or skipped-after-failure) and the command `ddflow merge X --force --reason "goldens pinned by lease, fixed on main"`, control reaches this block before anything else in the merge path and returns `O.refused("worktree.merged", ...)`. Either `force`/`reason` are parameters of this api function and the guard ignores them (the escape can never be taken), or they are not passed into the api at all, in which case no layer beneath the CLI can override the refusal and the documented `--force` path is dead. The accompanying knob doc in `config_sections/gates.py` corroborates the omission: it enumerates only "a run that passes, or `gate record --outcome unavailable|partial --reason`" as ways past, with no mention of `--force`. The regression test described ("merge with that state is refused") exercises only the refusing branch, so it would not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:101 (new `failed_ci_blockers` guard)

data.question: Do the ci/unit_tests prompts still say ci runs the whole suite?

evidence.note: commit on branch; 407 targeted tests pass; pins regenerated

chunk_findings.detail:
The change rewrites only `ddflow/services/gates/defs.py` (the ci `prompt` and the unit_tests `prompt`/`description`), but the test it edits still pins a third copy of the very claim being removed: the surrounding, untouched lines

```
assert "never record unit_tests from a run of\n  your own" in driver
assert "it runs the **whole** suite on the branch merged with the\n  base" in driver
```

require `driver` to keep stating that the ci stage runs the whole suite on the branch merged with the base. That is exactly the old precondition for the unit_tests coverage exception ("ci runs the WHOLE suite on the merge result and passes on this clean commit"), which the new prompts deliberately delete: the new ci text says that with `[ci].tests_scope = selected` (default) the run covers "only the ones your change reaches plus the `[ci].always_tests` guards", and the new unit_tests text says coverage is `covered by ci selected run <sha>` — i.e. coverage is now granted even though ci did *not* run the whole suite. So an agent that follows `driver` is told the whole suite is what runs on the merge result and is the precondition for recording unit_tests, while the gate prompts tell it the opposite; given the new default it will read the driver's precondition as unmet and handle the unit_tests gate incorrectly (e.g. insist on running the whole suite or refuse the `covered by ci selected run` record). Either `driver` is a third stale copy that the change must also reword (the change's stated goal — no gate text claims an item's ci runs the whole suite — is not achieved), or it is generated from the gate definitions, in which case this unchanged assertion now fails and breaks the test suite. Both outcomes are defects of this change; the diff does neither, so the contradiction survives and is frozen by the test.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated purpose of this change is that the **ci** prompt must stop claiming that an item's ci runs the whole suite ("the ci prompt lists 'the tests' as part of the pre-push stage"). For the unit_tests prompt the test adds a negative assertion (`assert "tests_scope = selected" in prompt and "WHOLE suite" not in prompt`, plus the description check), so a partial rewrite there fails. For the ci prompt it only adds positive assertions — `assert "tests_scope = selected" in ci and "always_tests" in ci` — and never asserts the removed claim is absent from `ci`. Concretely: if the ci prompt is left with a sentence such as "it runs the tests on the branch merged with the base" / a whole-suite clause anywhere (the exact defect this item exists to remove), both new assertions still pass (`"tests_scope = selected"` and `"always_tests"` can both be present alongside the stale sentence), and the regression this change is supposed to pin is not pinned for its primary target. The same asymmetry applies to `G.DEFAULT_GATES["ci"].description`, which is never checked at all. A `"WHOLE suite"-style negative assertion (or a check for the offending clause) on the ci prompt/description is what makes the test actually cover the change.

chunk_findings.detail:
The change is supposed to answer the earlier confirmed finding that the ci-prompt half of this test only added *positive* assertions, so a partial rewrite of the ci prompt (the prompt that per the stated intent "lists 'the tests' as part of the pre-push stage") could regress without the test failing. The "fix" adds `assert "WHOLE" not in ci and "the tests ..." not in ci`, but neither half actually guards the claim:

- `"the tests ..."` is a literal substring containing a space and three period characters. No plausible ci prompt contains a bare printing ellipsis; and the old complaint was the phrase `the tests`, not `the tests ...`. So for a ci prompt that reverts to saying the pre-push stage runs `the tests` (or anything other than that exact ellipsis token), the assertion still passes — given input `ci` whose pre-push stage text is "run the tests", line 177 returns without failing, which is exactly the regression the earlier finding said the test must catch. (The positive assertion the reworded prompt legitimately needs, "the tests the change reaches", is of course not asserted against either, which is presumably why the placeholder was used — but the placeholder guards nothing.)
- `"WHOLE"` is asserted without its lowercase counterpart, while the *unit_tests* side of the same test does check `"WHOLE suite"`. A ci prompt that says "the whole suite" is not caught, so the uppercase-only check only covers a phrasing the intent never attributed to the ci prompt in the first place.

So finding #1 still holds for the ci prompt: the added negatives are decorative and the test still cannot distinguish a correctly scoped ci prompt from one that claims the item's ci runs all tests.

chunk_findings.detail: The prior MEDIUM finding was that only the unit_tests prompt got negative assertions while the ci prompt got positive ones, so a partial rewrite of the ci prompt would still pass. The added negative assertion on the "the tests" side does not actually answer it. `"the tests ..."` is a plain-substring `in` check for a literal that includes a space followed by an ellipsis; that literal is test-author filler, not something a prose prompt contains verbatim. Any rewrite of the ci prompt that keeps the same meaning in different words — e.g. `ci: before pushing, run the tests for the touched paths` — passes the assertion, because the string `"the tests ..."` (space-ellipsis) never appears. So the exact thing the earlier finding was about ("the ci prompt lists 'the tests' as part of the pre-push stage") is still unguarded: a partial/paraphrased rewrite of the ci prompt is not caught by the test, only the `WHOLE` substring is guarded. The probe should assert the same concrete phrasing the unit_tests branch uses (e.g. `assert "the tests" not in ci` or a quoted sentence from the old prompt), not an ellipsis placeholder.

chunk_findings.detail: The prior MEDIUM finding was that only the unit_tests prompt got negative assertions while the ci prompt got positive ones, so a partial rewrite of the ci prompt would still pass. The added negative assertion on the "the tests" side does not actually answer it. `"the tests ..."` is a plain-substring `in` check for a literal that includes a space followed by an ellipsis; that literal is test-author filler, not something a prose prompt contains verbatim. Any rewrite of the ci prompt that keeps the same meaning in different words — e.g. `ci: before pushing, run the tests for the touched paths` — passes the assertion, because the string `"the tests ..."` (space-ellipsis) never appears. So the exact thing the earlier finding was about ("the ci prompt lists 'the tests' as part of the pre-push stage") is still unguarded: a partial/paraphrased rewrite of the ci prompt is not caught by the test, only the `WHOLE` substring is guarded. The probe should assert the same concrete phrasing the unit_tests branch uses (e.g. `assert "the tests" not in ci` or a quoted sentence from the old prompt), not an ellipsis placeholder.
